case_title: Sachidanand Thakur v. Union of India & Ors.
accused_occupation: Indian Army personnel (Guard Commander on security duty at time of offence)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; Army Act 1950 (other penalties; specific sections not stated)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (Army personnel); medical (post-mortem); recovery of fired cartridge cases matched to weapon; accused's remark on apprehension
confession: Oral remark 'MAINE JO KARNA THA KAR DIYA' made on apprehension; relied on by the Court to remove any doubt about culpability
aggravating_circumstances: Three shots fired at close range (8 to 10 ft) despite a warning that the person was a Quick Reaction Team member
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 (Court Martial); sentenced to life imprisonment plus other penalties under Army Act 1950
high_court_outcome: Writ petition under Art. 226 dismissed; Court Martial findings confirmed; recall application dismissed
neutral_facts: On the night of 6 January 2000, the accused was on security duty as guard commander at a technical battery area of an army unit, armed with a 7.62 mm self-loading rifle and 20 cartridges. Following a report that stones had been thrown at the guard hut, the security junior commissioned officer ordered a Quick Reaction Team to be summoned. The team reached the guard hut at about 10.30 p.m., where the vehicle was challenged by the sentry on duty. Team members got out and moved to the right and left to locate the person who had thrown the stones. The accused ran toward one team member, the victim, while another team member followed and warned that the person being run toward was a member of the Quick Reaction Team and should not be fired upon. Despite this warning, the accused fired three shots from a distance of 8 to 10 feet, killing the victim at the spot. The accused was quickly apprehended by a sentry and the security junior commissioned officer. When questioned about what had been done, the accused replied 'MAINE JO KARNA THA KAR DIYA'. Evidence presented included the testimony of several army personnel who witnessed the shooting, post-mortem observations regarding the firing distance, and empty cartridge cases lifted from the site that matched the issued weapon.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from gunshot fire (three shots fired at 8 to 10 ft)
premeditation_planning: Not stated as premeditation; Court Martial found the shooting deliberate, and this finding was upheld
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness evidence of Army personnel including PW.14's warning; post-mortem observations (PW.16) on firing distance; fired cartridge cases matching the issued weapon; accused's remark on apprehension
witness_credibility: Court did not separately assess witness credibility; it accepted the Court Martial's findings of fact as free of error
post_offence_conduct: Quickly apprehended at the scene; made the remark 'MAINE JO KARNA THA KAR DIYA' when questioned
trial_duration: offence: 6 January 2000; trial judgment: not given (Court Martial date not stated); High Court: 23 December 2005 (recall application dismissed 23 November 2005); Supreme Court: 19 October 2010
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: D.K. Thakur, D. Jha, Debasis Misra. Respondents (Union of India and others): P.P. Tripathi, ASG, with N.S. Sweety Manchanda, Anil Katiyar, Anuj Bhandari, D.S. Mahra
investigation_status: Accused apprehended on the spot; tried by Court Martial. Police FIR and charge sheet not stated
appeal_history: Trial (Court Martial): guilty under s.302 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: writ petition dismissed, findings confirmed, recall application dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Court Martial findings of fact were categoric and based on correct appreciation of evidence; interference by courts in such matters should be minimal
defence_argument: Killing was an accident arising from suspicion of a terrorist attack; offence under s.302 not made out
legal_principle_applied: Supreme Court declines to disturb concurrent findings of fact of Court Martial upheld by High Court, finding no error in them
judicial_aggravating_factors: Three shots fired despite warning that the person was a Quick Reaction Team member; remark on apprehension removed doubt about culpability
